newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed a lacklustre afternoon session weaker on Thursday after a strong start, seesawing in line with German bunds.

"Players have not got too much enthusiasm at the moment," one dealer said, adding the market was taking a wait-and-see attitude ahead of U.S. September producer prices and retail sales data on Friday which would offer important pointers on U.S. interest rates.
Early trade saw guilder bonds firming, building on Wednesday's gains as the domestic-driven market was cheered by Dutch August PPI data.
Guilder bonds tend to shrug off domestic data, but Thursday's news of unchanged August producer prices had given an added fillip to an already upbeat market, dealers said earlier.
However sentiment was later dented by softer bunds and bund futures, which drifted down amid news the German central bank had left interest rates unchanged.
Some dealers cited stronger-than-expected U.S. weekly jobless data as another undermining factor, although in themselves the figures would not have had much of an impact.
Dealers said there was little to no short-end action.
"There was a tiny bit of turnover in the 6.25 percent July 98, and some in September 2002s and 2007s," one dealer said.
By contrast the January 2006 was a major focus throughout the day, dealers said. The yield spread on the benchmark 10-year widened under bunds by almost two basis points.
One said he believed there had been interest from one buyer in particular, but was unable to say whether this was a domestic or foreign player.
"Overall the guilder market is more domestic-driven at the moment," he said.
